phase: Phase 7.0 — complete-cost court over the producer corpus (PDF_DEFLATE_REPLAY_RANS vs BYTE_RANS)
claim: Under the real complete-cost court (serialized .voldoc size, verify + byte-compare) PDF_DEFLATE_REPLAY_RANS beats BYTE_RANS on 3/23 locally generated files: qpdf-preserve-objectstreams.pdf (qpdf 11.3.0 transformer output) by 55,167 B (112,147 -> 56,980), hand-base2.pdf by 55,126 B, and _synthetic/flate.pdf by 13,189 B. It loses on all 5 Ghostscript variants and both qpdf compression variants, and declines on the 12 files with no replayable Flate lane (1 qpdf + 11 synthetic). Every one of the 23 auto winners verifies and materializes byte-for-byte. The corpus is locally generated and is not a population sample; qpdf and Ghostscript are transformers, not authoring applications.
dirty_note: No tracked modifications at measurement time. Two untracked files were added: tools/pdf-court.sh (driver) and this receipt.
command: docker compose run --rm --no-TTY dev sh -c 'sh tools/pdf-court.sh evidence/scratch/court evidence/corpus/phase7/*.pdf evidence/corpus/phase7/_synthetic/*'

determinism.note: Two consecutive tools/pdf-corpus.sh runs produced identical sha256 for all qpdf-*.pdf, hand-*.pdf and _synthetic/* files. The five gs-*.pdf outputs differ (embedded per-run /ID + timestamp); byte length and FlateDecode compressed_bytes are stable.
